messages:
incident-bot: Paging: detected elevated 5xx rate from prefix routing layer (service=prefix-router, error_rate=7.8% over 5m) — auto-escalation triggered. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-incident :rotating_light:

sam: ack — I'm taking triage. grabbing logs and linking the runbook. @jordan can you jump in for infra-side?

jordan: oncall here, ack. looking at traffic split — large spike from tenant:delta-ingest around 11:02 UTC, requests up x6 vs baseline. seeing KV cache churn and hot-prefix thrashing.

maria: customer-impact check: list shows 3 enterprise tenants with degraded tail latency > 2s and increased erroring. cs-bot pinged CSMs for Delta and Echo.

sam: immediate mitigation plan (proposal):
1) throttle tenant:delta-ingest to 30% of normal QPS (apply tenant-level shaping)
2) reduce global prefix-cache TTL for non-critical prefixes to 250ms to avoid KV explosion
3) enable prefix-cache bypass for tenant:delta-ingest (per-tenant bypass) to ensure correctness while we stabilize
4) rollback any recent routing rules for model-x that landed at 10:50

jordan: +1 to tenant-level shaping. I can push a policy via /ops/traffic with this command:```sh
opsctl traffic update --tenant delta-ingest --qps 0.3 --reason "mitigate prefix thrash"
```

emily: I'll cut a temporary quota change for Delta so they drop to 50% of committed throughput. Doing that now via console.

ops-bot: Executing traffic change: opsctl traffic update --tenant delta-ingest --qps 0.3 succeeded (job id 07b3f). Change propagated to edge routers in eu-west-1 and us-west-2.

sam: applying per-tenant prefix cache bypass: we will flip feature-flag prefix_bypass:delta-ingest. command:```sh
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/flags -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"flag":"prefix_bypass","tenant":"delta-ingest","value":true}'
```

jordan: applied. kernel metrics show prefix hit rate for tenant:delta-ingest fell to 2% (expected), KV write QPS dropped 78% in 3m. Error rate on prefix-router decreased to 3.1% after shaping.

maria: FYI CS updated: Delta's ingestion queue backed up ~15 minutes and some payloads retried; we've flagged for manual replay. No billing changes yet.

emily: lowered Delta quota to 50% of daily allowance. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/tenants/delta-ingest/quota

sam: also doing a targeted TTL rampdown for non-critical prefixes to protect KV store: policy change: set-prefix-ttl --match "prefix:public:*" --ttl 250ms. Will monitor.

ops-bot: TTL policy applied to 18k prefixes in 22s. CPU for KV-store nodes dropped 40% in 2m.

jordan: observed a small regression: certain composite prompts for Echo customers had correctness issues when bypassing prefix cache. Rolling a whitelist for critical customers to keep prefix cache on. Command:```sh
opsctl flags set prefix_bypass --tenant delta-ingest --whitelist "tenant:echo,tenant:alpha"````

sam: good catch. Added echo + alpha to whitelist. emily, coordinate with CS to confirm no customer-facing correctness regressions.

maria: CS confirms Echo and Alpha saw no new errors after whitelist. Delta will be asked to throttle ingest on their side; CSMs informed.

jordan: we also identified a recent deploy to model-x-router at 10:50 that increased request dispersion and uncovered a hot-prefix pattern. Rolling back that change to model-x-router v2.14.1 -> v2.14.0. Run rollback:```sh
ci deploy rollback model-x-router --from v2.14.1 --to v2.14.0 --reason "mitigate prefix hotspot"````

ops-bot: Rollback job 1f2a started. Canary pass ok on us-west-2 after 3m. Full rollout complete.

sam: after rollback + shaping + bypass, prefix-router errors now 0.9%, tail latency back within SLO for 95th. KV-store cpu normalized.

emily: kept throttle in place for 20 minutes to ensure stability, then gradually increased to 60% of previous QPS with monitoring guardrails.

maria: impact summary to include in incident doc:
- root cause: combination of sudden tenant:delta high fanout + recent model-x-router change exposing hot-prefix pattern
- customer impact: Delta ingestion delayed (queued ~15m), Echo/Alpha briefly exposed to bypass but whitelisted so no correctness impact
- mitigations: tenant-level shaping, per-tenant prefix bypass, prefix TTL rampdown, rollback model-x-router deploy, temporary tenant quota reduction

sam: handoff: @jordan I'm going offline in ~15m. @emily you own follow-up and action items: open postmortem, track Delta replay, evaluate prefix-ttl defaults, and propose permanent guardrails for tenant QPS spikes.

jordan: ack. I'll stay on for next 30m and then hand to night oncall. Next steps: add a circuit-breaker at prefix-router to auto-backoff on KV-store saturation and add a per-tenant burst budget check.

cs-bot: Notifying affected CSMs and customers: Delta, Echo, Alpha — messages queued.

sam: Thanks team — good coordination. Marking incident as mitigated. Full postmortem triage to follow. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident mitigated at 1771007650. Metrics baseline restored. Please update runbook with new mitigation knobs and add the circuit-breaker RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/prefix-circuit-breaker

jordan: filing follow-ups now: PRs for guardrails and TTL tuning in draft.

emily: creating the postmortem ticket and assigning action items. I'll include timeline and commands used.

maria: adding customer notes and replay plan to the incident doc.

sam: closing thread, will review postmortem draft tomorrow.
